east grinstead.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of mid Sussex
s1loc: East Grinstead's live scene runs through Chequer Mead, the purpose-built community theatre on De La Warr Road that stages more than 250 performances a year across drama, music and pantomime, with its Apron bar and the monthly East Grinstead Jazz Club. The East Grinstead Jazz Festival spreads live music across the town, from a jazz brunch at the Dorset Arms to an afternoon on the lawns at Chequer Mead, keeping a steady run of crew, stage and front-of-house work through the calendar.

And the trade here runs at two very different sizes. The bigger theatre operators, festival organisers and production companies run sizeable seasonal teams and order branded kit in volume through managed accounts, while independent crews, promoters and entertainers across mid Sussex want just a handful of embroidered polos or fleeces. A workwear supplier in this corner of West Sussex has to serve the busy festival weekend and the one-van crew alike, which is why we run trade accounts and direct online ordering together.

Beyond the main stage the town leans on Meridian Hall on College Lane for community gatherings, fairs and functions, while the East Grinstead Music and Arts Festival each spring brings singing, speech, drama and dance into local halls, and Sackville College runs its own seasonal events programme. Sitting where East Sussex, Kent, Surrey and West Sussex meet, the town also feeds crews out toward Crawley, Haywards Heath and Horsham, widening the catchment that needs branded event and steward kit.

didcot.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of south Oxfordshire
s1loc: Didcot's events anchor is the Cornerstone Arts Centre on Station Road, a purpose-built venue with a 220-seat auditorium, gallery and studios running comedy, drama, music and family shows the year round. Each summer the town fills out with the Didcot Festival of Cultures at Cornerstone, a free day of live performances, workshops and world food, plus the Music and Beer Festival, while the Didcot Railway Centre opens its 21-acre site around the 1932 engine shed for steam galas and seasonal events.

And the trade here splits clearly by size. The arts centre, the railway centre and the larger festival organisers and production companies run seasonal teams and order branded kit through managed accounts, while independent crews, promoters and entertainers across south Oxfordshire want only a few embroidered polos, fleeces or caps. A workwear supplier in this stretch of the county has to serve the big festival weekend and the single crew alike, which is why we keep trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

The wider calendar reaches well past the town centre, with the Didcot Food Festival each October drawing producers and street-food traders into the Civic Centre and the town square, and Didcot Civic Hall hosting community shows and fairs. Set on the main line between Oxford, Abingdon and Newbury, Didcot pulls event and steward work from across the Vale and the Thames corridor, so crews kitted here turn up at venues and showgrounds right across south Oxfordshire and beyond.

melton mowbray.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of the food capital
s1loc: Melton Mowbray trades on its food heritage, and the events to match. The Melton Mowbray Cattle Market hosts the East Midlands Food Festival each October, a long-running show pulling around 9,000 visitors and roughly 175 exhibitors with a Food Theatre, street-food area and live music, plus PieFest and SpiritsFest. The Melton Theatre, part of Brooksby Melton College on Asfordby Road, runs the indoor side with bands, pantomime, drama and dance through a refurbished auditorium.

And the trade here works at two scales. The big festival organisers, the cattle market operation and the touring production companies run large seasonal crews and order branded kit through managed accounts, while independent crews, market traders, promoters and entertainers across Leicestershire want just a few embroidered polos or fleeces. A workwear supplier in the home of the pork pie has to serve the packed food-festival weekend and the single crew alike, which is why we run trade accounts and direct online ordering together.

The food calendar runs well beyond October, with the Melton Mowbray Food Festival and the East Midlands Chilli Festival keeping stalls, demo stages and crews busy, while Melton Country Park gives the town its green space for outdoor gatherings and Brooksby Hall opens its parkland for seasonal events. As one of the licensed homes of Stilton and the famous pork pie, Melton draws traders and event teams from across the county and out toward Leicester, Loughborough and Grantham.

clydebank.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of West Dunbartonshire
s1loc: Clydebank's grand civic venue is Clydebank Town Hall on Hall Street, opened in 1902 and a survivor of the Clydebank Blitz, whose refurbished Grand Hall takes 600 standing for live gigs, comedy nights, fashion shows and conferences, backed by the Reception Hall, Ceremony Room and Garden Gallery for smaller functions. With Glasgow next door, the town sits inside one of the busiest live-events catchments in Scotland, feeding a steady run of stage, crew and front-of-house work.

And the trade here runs at two sizes. The town hall operation, the festival organisers and the production companies on the Clyde corridor run seasonal teams and order branded kit through managed accounts, while independent crews, promoters and entertainers across West Dunbartonshire want just a few embroidered polos or fleeces. A workwear supplier on this stretch of the river has to serve the packed hall night and the single crew alike, which is why we keep trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

The town's identity is bound to the Clyde and the John Brown shipyard, where the Category A-listed Titan Crane still stands over the waterfront beside Queens Quay, a focal point for outdoor and heritage events. Community celebrations and gatherings carry on at Dalmuir Park and the Town Hall through the year, and with Glasgow, Paisley and Dumbarton all close at hand, Clydebank crews work venues and showgrounds right across the west of Scotland.

kingswinford.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of the Glass Quarter
s1loc: Kingswinford sits at the edge of Stourbridge's historic Glass Quarter, and its events trade leans on that heritage. The International Festival of Glass runs every two years across the quarter with exhibitions, masterclasses, demonstrations and hundreds of artists, while the Stourbridge Glass Museum at Wordsley anchors the year-round programme. Closer to home the town stages live country music at DK Rugby Club, keeping a local run of stage, crew and front-of-house work through the season.

And the trade here works at two scales. The festival organisers, the museum operation and the production companies serving the borough run seasonal crews and order branded kit through managed accounts, while independent crews, promoters and entertainers across the Dudley borough want just a few embroidered polos or fleeces. A workwear supplier in this part of the West Midlands has to serve the busy festival weekend and the single crew alike, which is why we keep trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

The old Broadfield House in Kingswinford once held the glass collection now shown at the Stourbridge Glass Museum, and the Glass Quarter heritage trail still draws walking tours and cultural events along the Stourbridge Canal.
